The **2018–19 Premier League** was the 27th [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_(sports) "Season (sports)") of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 120th season of top-flight English football overall. The season started on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 12 May 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-3) Fixtures for the 2018–19 season were announced on 14 June 2018. The league was contested by the top 17 teams from the 2017–18 season as well as [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C."), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), who joined as the promoted clubs from the [2017–18 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). They replaced [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_F.C. "Swansea City F.C.") and [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") who were relegated to the [2018–19 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-4)

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") were the defending champions, and they won their fourth Premier League title, and sixth English top-flight title overall, retaining the title on the last day of the season with 98 points after winning their last 14 league games. [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") finished second with 97 points – the highest total in English top-flight history for a second-placed team.

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") claimed the league title on the last day of the season with a 4–1 win at [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C."), finishing on 98 points after a run of 14 straight wins.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-5)[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") held a 7-point lead over Manchester City on 3 January,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-6) but finished runners-up with 97 points – the fourth highest total in Premier League history and the highest in English top-flight history for a second-placed team, having lost only one league match all season – to eventual champions City.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

[Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") claimed the other two Champions League berths, finishing in third and fourth place respectively. Tottenham were in third place for much of the season and were considered potential title challengers until a 1–2 loss to [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") in February.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Chelsea would go on to win the season's [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018-19_UEFA_Europa_League "2018-19 UEFA Europa League"), defeating [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in the final 4–1. Arsenal had gone on a fourteen-game unbeaten run near the start of the season and began April in third place, but a run of four points in six matches saw them drop to fifth place, finishing outside of the Champions League spots.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

[Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.")'s worst start to the season for 28 years and 3–1 loss to Liverpool led to the sacking of manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") in December,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-10) with former player [Ole Gunnar Solskjær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Gunnar_Solskj%C3%A6r "Ole Gunnar Solskjær") replacing him, initially as a caretaker. Solskjær was appointed permanently after an impressive run of results which culminated in United's away goals victory over [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint_Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint Germain F.C.") in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-11) but the team's poor form soon returned, and they eventually finished sixth after the team had won none of their final five league matches.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-12) Newly promoted [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") achieved their highest finish since 1980 by finishing seventh, having taken points off every team in the league except Liverpool and [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C.").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-13) Their seventh-place finish was the highest for a newly promoted team since [Ipswich Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich_Town_F.C. "Ipswich Town F.C.") finished 5th in the [2000–01 season.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_in_English_football "2000–01 in English football")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-14)

Huddersfield were the first team to be relegated, following their 0–2 defeat at [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C.") on 30 March 2019, coinciding with victories for [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."). They were relegated with six games remaining. This made Huddersfield the second team in Premier League history to be relegated before March ended, following [Derby County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derby_County_F.C. "Derby County F.C.") in [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Premier_League "2007–08 Premier League").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-15) Fulham joined them after a 1–4 defeat at [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") on 2 April, relegated with five games remaining.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-16)[Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") were the final team to be relegated following a 2–3 loss at home to Crystal Palace on 4 May with one game remaining.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-17)

The fastest goal in Premier League history was scored this season on 23 April by [Shane Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Long "Shane Long") in a 1–1 draw between his side [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") and [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") after 7.69 seconds.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-19) On 4 May 2019, Fulham's [Harvey Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Elliott "Harvey Elliott") became the youngest ever Premier League player at 16 years and 30 days.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-20) Tottenham Hotspur had a run of 28 games without a draw (20 wins, 8 losses), the longest ever recorded from the start of a Premier League season.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-21) Manchester City finished the season without a draw in any of their final [30 matches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#Fixtures "2018–19 Manchester City F.C. season").

The season saw two aviation incidents involving Premier League personnel. On 27 October 2018, [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") owner [Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichai_Srivaddhanaprabha "Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha") was killed in a [helicopter crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Leicester_helicopter_crash "2018 Leicester helicopter crash") outside the [King Power Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Power_Stadium "King Power Stadium"), shortly after a 1–1 home draw against [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."). Almost three months later, on 21 January 2019, Cardiff City player [Emiliano Sala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Sala "Emiliano Sala"), en route to join the club following [his record signing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_Emiliano_Sala_from_FC_Nantes_to_Cardiff_City_F.C. "Transfer of Emiliano Sala from FC Nantes to Cardiff City F.C.") from [Nantes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Nantes "FC Nantes"), died on board a Piper PA-46 Malibu aircraft that [crashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Piper_PA-46_Malibu_crash "2019 Piper PA-46 Malibu crash") off [Alderney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderney "Alderney").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-BBC-22)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). The promoted teams were [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") (returning after a six-year absence), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") (both teams returning after a four-year absence). They replaced [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C."), [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") and [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), who were relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship") after their top flight spells of seven, ten and eight years respectively.

The **2018–19 Premier League** was the 27th [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_(sports) "Season (sports)") of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 120th season of top-flight English football overall. The season started on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 12 May 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-3) Fixtures for the 2018–19 season were announced on 14 June 2018. The league was contested by the top 17 teams from the 2017–18 season as well as [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C."), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), who joined as the promoted clubs from the [2017–18 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). They replaced [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_F.C. "Swansea City F.C.") and [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") who were relegated to the [2018–19 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-4)

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") were the defending champions, and they won their fourth Premier League title, and sixth English top-flight title overall, retaining the title on the last day of the season with 98 points after winning their last 14 league games. [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") finished second with 97 points – the highest total in English top-flight history for a second-placed team.

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") claimed the league title on the last day of the season with a 4–1 win at [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C."), finishing on 98 points after a run of 14 straight wins.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-5)[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") held a 7-point lead over Manchester City on 3 January,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-6) but finished runners-up with 97 points – the fourth highest total in Premier League history and the highest in English top-flight history for a second-placed team, having lost only one league match all season – to eventual champions City.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

[Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") claimed the other two Champions League berths, finishing in third and fourth place respectively. Tottenham were in third place for much of the season and were considered potential title challengers until a 1–2 loss to [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") in February.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Chelsea would go on to win the season's [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018-19_UEFA_Europa_League "2018-19 UEFA Europa League"), defeating [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in the final 4–1. Arsenal had gone on a fourteen-game unbeaten run near the start of the season and began April in third place, but a run of four points in six matches saw them drop to fifth place, finishing outside of the Champions League spots.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

[Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.")'s worst start to the season for 28 years and 3–1 loss to Liverpool led to the sacking of manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") in December,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-10) with former player [Ole Gunnar Solskjær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Gunnar_Solskj%C3%A6r "Ole Gunnar Solskjær") replacing him, initially as a caretaker. Solskjær was appointed permanently after an impressive run of results which culminated in United's away goals victory over [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint_Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint Germain F.C.") in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-11) but the team's poor form soon returned, and they eventually finished sixth after the team had won none of their final five league matches.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-12) Newly promoted [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") achieved their highest finish since 1980 by finishing seventh, having taken points off every team in the league except Liverpool and [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C.").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-13) Their seventh-place finish was the highest for a newly promoted team since [Ipswich Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich_Town_F.C. "Ipswich Town F.C.") finished 5th in the [2000–01 season.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_in_English_football "2000–01 in English football")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-14)

Huddersfield were the first team to be relegated, following their 0–2 defeat at [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C.") on 30 March 2019, coinciding with victories for [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."). They were relegated with six games remaining. This made Huddersfield the second team in Premier League history to be relegated before March ended, following [Derby County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derby_County_F.C. "Derby County F.C.") in [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Premier_League "2007–08 Premier League").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-15) Fulham joined them after a 1–4 defeat at [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") on 2 April, relegated with five games remaining.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-16)[Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") were the final team to be relegated following a 2–3 loss at home to Crystal Palace on 4 May with one game remaining.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-17)

The fastest goal in Premier League history was scored this season on 23 April by [Shane Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Long "Shane Long") in a 1–1 draw between his side [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") and [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") after 7.69 seconds.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-19) On 4 May 2019, Fulham's [Harvey Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Elliott "Harvey Elliott") became the youngest ever Premier League player at 16 years and 30 days.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-20) Tottenham Hotspur had a run of 28 games without a draw (20 wins, 8 losses), the longest ever recorded from the start of a Premier League season.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-21) Manchester City finished the season without a draw in any of their final [30 matches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#Fixtures "2018–19 Manchester City F.C. season").

The season saw two aviation incidents involving Premier League personnel. On 27 October 2018, [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") owner [Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichai_Srivaddhanaprabha "Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha") was killed in a [helicopter crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Leicester_helicopter_crash "2018 Leicester helicopter crash") outside the [King Power Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Power_Stadium "King Power Stadium"), shortly after a 1–1 home draw against [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."). Almost three months later, on 21 January 2019, Cardiff City player [Emiliano Sala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Sala "Emiliano Sala"), en route to join the club following [his record signing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_Emiliano_Sala_from_FC_Nantes_to_Cardiff_City_F.C. "Transfer of Emiliano Sala from FC Nantes to Cardiff City F.C.") from [Nantes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Nantes "FC Nantes"), died on board a Piper PA-46 Malibu aircraft that [crashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Piper_PA-46_Malibu_crash "2019 Piper PA-46 Malibu crash") off [Alderney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderney "Alderney").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-BBC-22)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). The promoted teams were [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") (returning after a six-year absence), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") (both teams returning after a four-year absence). They replaced [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C."), [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") and [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), who were relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship") after their top flight spells of seven, ten and eight years respectively.

The **2018–19 [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A")** (known as the **Serie A [TIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecom_Italia "Telecom Italia")** for sponsorship reasons) was the 117th season of top-tier Italian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), the 87th in a [round-robin tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"), and the 9th since its organization under a league committee separate from [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B"). [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") were the seven-time defending champions and defended their title following their victory against [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") on 20 April 2019. The season was run from 18 August 2018 to 26 May 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-2)

## Events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Events")]

[Hellas Verona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellas_Verona_F.C. "Hellas Verona F.C.") and [Benevento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benevento_Calcio "Benevento Calcio") immediately returned to [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_B "2018–19 Serie B") after finishing 19th and 20th while [Crotone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F.C._Crotone "F.C. Crotone"), finishing in 18th place, were relegated after two seasons in the top flight.

On 28 April, [Empoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empoli_F.C. "Empoli F.C.") earned the right to come back to Serie A after one year of relegation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-3) On 18 May 2018, [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") achieved promotion having finished second in the [2017–18 Serie B season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Serie_B "2017–18 Serie B"), just three seasons after their bankruptcy relegation to [Serie D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_D "Serie D").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-4) The last team promoted, after 2 years of absence, was [Frosinone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frosinone_Calcio "Frosinone Calcio"), who defeated [Palermo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Citt%C3%A0_di_Palermo "U.S. Città di Palermo") in the Serie B play-off finals 3–2 on aggregate.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-5)

On 23 July, [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") were handed a 5-point deduction for the 2018–19 Serie A season, following text messages from Parma player [Emanuele Calaiò](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emanuele_Calai%C3%B2 "Emanuele Calaiò") "eliciting a reduced effort" from two players of [Spezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spezia_Calcio "Spezia Calcio") during the 2017–18 season, a match [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") won 2–0 to secure promotion to this season.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-6) On 9 August, [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") had the 5-point deduction expunged.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-7)

On 14 August, the day of the [Ponte Morandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponte_Morandi "Ponte Morandi") bridge collapse in Genoa, the [Italian Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Football_Federation "Italian Football Federation") announced a minute's silence would be added for the victims of the collapse before all Serie A matches during the opening weekend that succeeded the incident.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-8) On 16 August, the [Lega Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A") postponed the opening matches for both Genoese clubs [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa_C.F.C. "Genoa C.F.C.") and [Sampdoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.C._Sampdoria "U.C. Sampdoria") that were originally scheduled for 19 August.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-9)

On 13 September, Chievo was deducted 3 points after being found guilty of false accounting.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-10)

On 14 April 2019, Chievo was relegated from Serie A after a 3–1 defeat by Napoli, ending an eleven-year spell in the top flight.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-11)

On 20 April, Juventus won their 35th title and their eighth in a row with a win over Fiorentina.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-12)

On 5 May, Frosinone was relegated from Serie A after a 2–2 draw away at Sassuolo, going down after just one season.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-13)

On 26 May, [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_B.C. "Atalanta B.C.") finished third and secured a place in the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Champions_League "2019–20 UEFA Champions League") group stage, both for the first time in their history.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-14) Meanwhile, Empoli which were one point above the relegation zone ahead of Genoa, were eventually relegated to Serie B after they were defeated by [Internazionale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan"), while Genoa drew with [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina").

This was also the last season of iconic [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Roma "A.S. Roma") captain [Daniele De Rossi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniele_De_Rossi "Daniele De Rossi") that left the team after 18 seasons,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-15) while veterans [Sergio Pellissier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Pellissier "Sergio Pellissier") (from [Chievo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._ChievoVerona "A.C. The **2018–19 [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A")** (known as the **Serie A [TIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecom_Italia "Telecom Italia")** for sponsorship reasons) was the 117th season of top-tier Italian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), the 87th in a [round-robin tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"), and the 9th since its organization under a league committee separate from [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B"). [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") were the seven-time defending champions and defended their title following their victory against [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") on 20 April 2019. The season was run from 18 August 2018 to 26 May 2019.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-2)

## Events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Events")]

[Hellas Verona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellas_Verona_F.C. "Hellas Verona F.C.") and [Benevento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benevento_Calcio "Benevento Calcio") immediately returned to [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_B "2018–19 Serie B") after finishing 19th and 20th while [Crotone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F.C._Crotone "F.C. Crotone"), finishing in 18th place, were relegated after two seasons in the top flight.

On 28 April, [Empoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empoli_F.C. "Empoli F.C.") earned the right to come back to Serie A after one year of relegation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-3) On 18 May 2018, [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") achieved promotion having finished second in the [2017–18 Serie B season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Serie_B "2017–18 Serie B"), just three seasons after their bankruptcy relegation to [Serie D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_D "Serie D").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-4) The last team promoted, after 2 years of absence, was [Frosinone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frosinone_Calcio "Frosinone Calcio"), who defeated [Palermo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Citt%C3%A0_di_Palermo "U.S. Città di Palermo") in the Serie B play-off finals 3–2 on aggregate.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-5)

On 23 July, [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") were handed a 5-point deduction for the 2018–19 Serie A season, following text messages from Parma player [Emanuele Calaiò](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emanuele_Calai%C3%B2 "Emanuele Calaiò") "eliciting a reduced effort" from two players of [Spezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spezia_Calcio "Spezia Calcio") during the 2017–18 season, a match [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") won 2–0 to secure promotion to this season.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-6) On 9 August, [Parma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parma_Calcio_1913 "Parma Calcio 1913") had the 5-point deduction expunged.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-7)

On 14 August, the day of the [Ponte Morandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponte_Morandi "Ponte Morandi") bridge collapse in Genoa, the [Italian Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Football_Federation "Italian Football Federation") announced a minute's silence would be added for the victims of the collapse before all Serie A matches during the opening weekend that succeeded the incident.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-8) On 16 August, the [Lega Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A") postponed the opening matches for both Genoese clubs [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa_C.F.C. "Genoa C.F.C.") and [Sampdoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.C._Sampdoria "U.C. Sampdoria") that were originally scheduled for 19 August.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-9)

On 13 September, Chievo was deducted 3 points after being found guilty of false accounting.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-10)

On 14 April 2019, Chievo was relegated from Serie A after a 3–1 defeat by Napoli, ending an eleven-year spell in the top flight.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-11)

On 20 April, Juventus won their 35th title and their eighth in a row with a win over Fiorentina.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-12)

On 5 May, Frosinone was relegated from Serie A after a 2–2 draw away at Sassuolo, going down after just one season.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-13)

On 26 May, [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_B.C. "Atalanta B.C.") finished third and secured a place in the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_UEFA_Champions_League "2019–20 UEFA Champions League") group stage, both for the first time in their history.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-14) Meanwhile, Empoli which were one point above the relegation zone ahead of Genoa, were eventually relegated to Serie B after they were defeated by [Internazionale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan"), while Genoa drew with [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina").

This was also the last season of iconic [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Roma "A.S. Roma") captain [Daniele De Rossi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniele_De_Rossi "Daniele De Rossi") that left the team after 18 seasons,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-15) while veterans [Sergio Pellissier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Pellissier "Sergio Pellissier") (from [Chievo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._ChievoVerona "A.C. ChievoVerona")),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-16)[Andrea Barzagli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Barzagli "Andrea Barzagli") (from [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC"))[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-17) and [Emiliano Moretti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Moretti "Emiliano Moretti") (from [Torino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torino_F.C. "Torino F.C."))[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Serie_A#cite_note-18) retired from professional football at the end of the season.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Football tournament

The **2018–19 UEFA Champions League group stage** began on 18 September and ended on 12 December 2018.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-calendar-1) A total of 32 teams competed in the group stage to decide the 16 places in the [knockout phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase") of the [2018–19 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

## Draw

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Draw")]

The draw for the group stage was held on 30 August 2018, 18:00 [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time"), at the [Grimaldi Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimaldi_Forum "Grimaldi Forum") in [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-GS_draw-3)

The 32 teams were drawn into eight groups of four, with the restriction that teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other. For the draw, the teams were seeded into four pots based on the following principles (Regulations Article 13.06):[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

*   Pot 1 contained the Champions League title holders, the Europa League title holders, and the champions of the top six associations based on their 2017 [UEFA country coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_Association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-country_coefficients-4) If either the Champions League or Europa League title holders were one of the champions of the top six associations, the champions of the association ranked seventh (and possibly eighth) were also seeded into Pot 1.
*   Pot 2, 3 and 4 contained the remaining teams, seeded based on their 2018 [UEFA club coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_Club_coefficient "UEFA coefficient").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-club_coefficients-5)

On 17 July 2014, the UEFA emergency panel ruled that Ukrainian and Russian clubs would not be drawn against each other "until further notice" due to the [political unrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_pro-Russian_unrest_in_Ukraine "2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine") between the countries.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-6)

Moreover, the draw was controlled for teams from the same association in order to split the teams evenly into the two sets of four groups (A–D, E–H) for maximum television coverage. On each matchday, one set of four groups played their matches on Tuesday, while the other set of four groups played their matches on Wednesday, with the two sets of groups alternating between each matchday. The fixtures were decided after the draw, using a computer draw not shown to public, with the following match sequence (Regulations Article 16.02):[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

Group stage schedule| Matchday | Dates | Matches[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-8) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matchday 1 | 18–19 September 2018 | 2 v 3, 4 v 1 |
| Matchday 2 | 2–3 October 2018 | 1 v 2, 3 v 4 |
| Matchday 3 | 23–24 October 2018 | 3 v 1, 2 v 4 |
| Matchday 4 | 6–7 November 2018 | 1 v 3, 4 v 2 |
| Matchday 5 | 27–28 November 2018 | 3 v 2, 1 v 4 |
| Matchday 6 | 11–12 December 2018 | 2 v 1, 4 v 3 |

There were scheduling restrictions: for example, teams from the same city (e.g. [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") and [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid")) in general were not scheduled to play at home on the same matchday (to avoid them playing at home on the same day or on consecutive days, due to logistics and crowd control), and teams from "winter countries" (e.g. Russia) were not scheduled to play at home on the last matchday (due to cold weather).

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Format")]

In each group, teams played against each other home-and-away in a [round-robin format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"). The group winners and runners-up advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"), while the third-placed teams entered the [Europa League round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").

### Tiebreakers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tiebreakers")]

Teams were ranked according to [points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, 0 points for a loss), and if tied on points, the following tiebreaking criteria were applied, in the order given, to determine the rankings (Regulations Articles 17.01):[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

1.   Points in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
2.   [Goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference") in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
3.   Goals scored in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
4.   [Away goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") scored in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
5.   If more than two teams were tied, and after applying all head-to-head criteria above, a subset of teams were still tied, all head-to-head criteria above was reapplied exclusively to this subset of teams;
6.   Goal difference in all group matches;
7.   Goals scored in all group matches;
8.   Away goals scored in all group matches;
9.   Wins in all group matches;
10.   Away wins in all group matches;
11.   Disciplinary points (red card = 3 points, yellow card = 1 point, expulsion for two yellow cards in one match = 3 points);
12.   [UEFA club coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_coefficient "UEFA club coefficient").

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Football tournament

The **2018–19 UEFA Champions League group stage** began on 18 September and ended on 12 December 2018.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-calendar-1) A total of 32 teams competed in the group stage to decide the 16 places in the [knockout phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase") of the [2018–19 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

## Draw

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Draw")]

The draw for the group stage was held on 30 August 2018, 18:00 [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time"), at the [Grimaldi Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimaldi_Forum "Grimaldi Forum") in [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-GS_draw-3)

The 32 teams were drawn into eight groups of four, with the restriction that teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other. For the draw, the teams were seeded into four pots based on the following principles (Regulations Article 13.06):[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

*   Pot 1 contained the Champions League title holders, the Europa League title holders, and the champions of the top six associations based on their 2017 [UEFA country coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_Association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-country_coefficients-4) If either the Champions League or Europa League title holders were one of the champions of the top six associations, the champions of the association ranked seventh (and possibly eighth) were also seeded into Pot 1.
*   Pot 2, 3 and 4 contained the remaining teams, seeded based on their 2018 [UEFA club coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_Club_coefficient "UEFA coefficient").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-club_coefficients-5)

On 17 July 2014, the UEFA emergency panel ruled that Ukrainian and Russian clubs would not be drawn against each other "until further notice" due to the [political unrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_pro-Russian_unrest_in_Ukraine "2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine") between the countries.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-6)

Moreover, the draw was controlled for teams from the same association in order to split the teams evenly into the two sets of four groups (A–D, E–H) for maximum television coverage. On each matchday, one set of four groups played their matches on Tuesday, while the other set of four groups played their matches on Wednesday, with the two sets of groups alternating between each matchday. The fixtures were decided after the draw, using a computer draw not shown to public, with the following match sequence (Regulations Article 16.02):[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

Group stage schedule| Matchday | Dates | Matches[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-8) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matchday 1 | 18–19 September 2018 | 2 v 3, 4 v 1 |
| Matchday 2 | 2–3 October 2018 | 1 v 2, 3 v 4 |
| Matchday 3 | 23–24 October 2018 | 3 v 1, 2 v 4 |
| Matchday 4 | 6–7 November 2018 | 1 v 3, 4 v 2 |
| Matchday 5 | 27–28 November 2018 | 3 v 2, 1 v 4 |
| Matchday 6 | 11–12 December 2018 | 2 v 1, 4 v 3 |

There were scheduling restrictions: for example, teams from the same city (e.g. [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") and [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid")) in general were not scheduled to play at home on the same matchday (to avoid them playing at home on the same day or on consecutive days, due to logistics and crowd control), and teams from "winter countries" (e.g. Russia) were not scheduled to play at home on the last matchday (due to cold weather).

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Format")]

In each group, teams played against each other home-and-away in a [round-robin format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"). The group winners and runners-up advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"), while the third-placed teams entered the [Europa League round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2018–19 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").

### Tiebreakers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tiebreakers")]

Teams were ranked according to [points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, 0 points for a loss), and if tied on points, the following tiebreaking criteria were applied, in the order given, to determine the rankings (Regulations Articles 17.01):[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-2)

1.   Points in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
2.   [Goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference") in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
3.   Goals scored in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
4.   [Away goals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") scored in head-to-head matches among tied teams;
5.   If more than two teams were tied, and after applying all head-to-head criteria above, a subset of teams were still tied, all head-to-head criteria above was reapplied exclusively to this subset of teams;
6.   Goal difference in all group matches;
7.   Goals scored in all group matches;
8.   Away goals scored in all group matches;
9.   Wins in all group matches;
10.   Away wins in all group matches;
11.   Disciplinary points (red card = 3 points, yellow card = 1 point, expulsion for two yellow cards in one match = 3 points);
12.   [UEFA club coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_coefficient "UEFA club coefficient").

The **2018–19 season** was [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.")'s [117th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Manchester_City_F.C._seasons "List of Manchester City F.C. seasons") of competitive [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), 90th season in the [top flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system "English football league system") of [English football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_England "Football in England") and 22nd season in the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-1) In addition to the league, the club competed in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"), [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_FA_Cup "2018–19 FA Cup"), [EFL Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup"), and [FA Community Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FA_Community_Shield "2018 FA Community Shield"); for the Champions League, it was their eighth consecutive season competing in the tournament. The season covered the period from 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2019.

During this season, City completed a [domestic treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Domestic_trebles "Treble (association football)"). Apart from winning all three of the major English football tournaments, they also won the Community Shield, the first time any team has ever held all four of England's primary football trophies at the same time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-2) The season was the first since [2009–10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Manchester_City_F.C._season "2009–10 Manchester City F.C. season") without [Yaya Touré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaya_Tour%C3%A9 "Yaya Touré"), who departed to [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C."), and the first since [2005–06](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Manchester_City_F.C._season "2005–06 Manchester City F.C. season") without [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart"), who joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") after two seasons of loans.

## Season summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Season summary")]

In the 2018–19 season, Manchester City maintained their free scoring form under manager [Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola") and became the first club in Europe's top leagues to pass 100 goals scored on 20 January 2019 when [Danilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danilo_(footballer,_born_July_1991) "Danilo (footballer, born July 1991)") scored the first goal in City's 3–0 victory at [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_F.C. "Huddersfield Town F.C.").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-3)

City went on to break their own record for a top flight English club for goals scored in all competitions in a season. [Leroy Sané](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leroy_San%C3%A9 "Leroy Sané")'s goal in City's 2–0 win at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") on 24 April 2019 overtook the previous record tally of 156, which was established by [Manuel Pellegrini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Pellegrini "Manuel Pellegrini")'s City side back in their title-winning [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Manchester_City_F.C._season "2013–14 Manchester City F.C. season").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-4) By the end of the 2018–19 season, the team reached 169 goals scored.

[![Image 93](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Chelsea_vs_Man_City_2019-02-24.svg/250px-Chelsea_vs_Man_City_2019-02-24.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chelsea_vs_Man_City_2019-02-24.svg)

Line-ups for the [2019 EFL Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_EFL_Cup_final "2019 EFL Cup final") between Chelsea and Manchester City

On 24 February, City won their sixth [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup") title when they defeated [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C "Chelsea F.C") 4–3 on penalties after a goalless draw over 120 minutes at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-5)

Expectations were high for City's [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League") campaign. The team again won their group without breaking a sweat, then routed [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04") in the round of 16, winning their home match 7–0. Similar to the previous season, City were drawn against an English club in the quarter-finals, this time [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."). _The Blues_ dropped their away match 0–1, with [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") missing a penalty. The home match was all-or-nothing for City and it proved to be one of the best matches of that season. [Raheem Sterling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raheem_Sterling "Raheem Sterling") scored in the beginning, but City quickly conceded two goals and now needed to score three to advance. The squad did exactly that, leading 4–2 with 20 minutes to play. However, [Fernando Llorente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Llorente "Fernando Llorente")'s contentious goal for Spurs meant City again needed a goal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-6) In added time, Sterling converted a pass from Agüero and the entire stadium started celebrating what seemed to be a certain victory. However, the goal was disallowed after a VAR review and _the Blues_ were eliminated in a heartbreaking fashion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-7)

The 2018–19 Premier League title race was one of the closest contests of the Premier League era. City and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") exchanged their leads 32 times over the season, in part due to fixture rearrangements for [EFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup") and [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_FA_Cup "2018–19 FA Cup") matches and television demands. The two title contenders jointly amassed a combined total of 195 points, which at the time was the highest combined total in English top flight history.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-8)

On 12 May, City won their final league match of the league season 4–1 away at [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.") to retain the Premier League title. In doing so, they matched their own record for 32 wins over a single season. They had to win their final 14 consecutive league matches to hold off the challenge of Liverpool, who themselves ended their season with nine-straight wins.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-9)

One week later, on 18 May, City defeated [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") 6–0 at Wembley [to win the FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_FA_Cup_Final "2019 FA Cup Final") and complete an unprecedented English men's [domestic treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Domestic_trebles "Treble (association football)") and clean sweep of the major honors in English football. It was also City's first ever league and FA Cup [double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)") and their sixth overall FA Cup title. The 6–0 scoreline was also the joint largest winning margin in the history of the FA Cup Final and the largest for any final in the competition since [1903](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1903_FA_Cup_Final "1903 FA Cup Final").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-10) This final win of the season was Manchester City's 50th in all competitions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-11)

As of 9 April 2019, Manchester City had won the Carabao Cup, progressed to the final of the FA Cup, were in second place with one game in hand in the Premier League and scheduled to play Tottenham in the Champions League quarter-finals, thus making it possible to achieve the [quadruple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_football_teams_to_have_won_four_or_more_trophies_in_one_season "List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season"), a unique sweep of four major tournaments in a single season, something that had not been done by any English men's side. A win in each of City’s last twelve games of the season (potential UCL semi-finals and [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2019 UEFA Champions League Final") included) would have guaranteed the quadruple for the club. However, a dramatic loss to Tottenham on away goals on 17 April ended City's quadruple hopes. Still, the Blues managed to achieve an unprecedented domestic treble.

The **2018–19 season** was [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.")'s [117th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Manchester_City_F.C._seasons "List of Manchester City F.C. seasons") of competitive [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), 90th season in the [top flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_football_league_system "English football league system") of [English football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_England "Football in England") and 22nd season in the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-1) In addition to the league, the club competed in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"), [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_FA_Cup "2018–19 FA Cup"), [EFL Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup"), and [FA Community Shield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FA_Community_Shield "2018 FA Community Shield"); for the Champions League, it was their eighth consecutive season competing in the tournament. The season covered the period from 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2019.

During this season, City completed a [domestic treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Domestic_trebles "Treble (association football)"). Apart from winning all three of the major English football tournaments, they also won the Community Shield, the first time any team has ever held all four of England's primary football trophies at the same time.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-2) The season was the first since [2009–10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Manchester_City_F.C._season "2009–10 Manchester City F.C. season") without [Yaya Touré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yaya_Tour%C3%A9 "Yaya Touré"), who departed to [Olympiacos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympiacos_F.C. "Olympiacos F.C."), and the first since [2005–06](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Manchester_City_F.C._season "2005–06 Manchester City F.C. season") without [Joe Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hart "Joe Hart"), who joined [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") after two seasons of loans.

## Season summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Season summary")]

In the 2018–19 season, Manchester City maintained their free scoring form under manager [Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola") and became the first club in Europe's top leagues to pass 100 goals scored on 20 January 2019 when [Danilo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danilo_(footballer,_born_July_1991) "Danilo (footballer, born July 1991)") scored the first goal in City's 3–0 victory at [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_F.C. "Huddersfield Town F.C.").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-3)

City went on to break their own record for a top flight English club for goals scored in all competitions in a season. [Leroy Sané](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leroy_San%C3%A9 "Leroy Sané")'s goal in City's 2–0 win at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") on 24 April 2019 overtook the previous record tally of 156, which was established by [Manuel Pellegrini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Pellegrini "Manuel Pellegrini")'s City side back in their title-winning [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Manchester_City_F.C._season "2013–14 Manchester City F.C. season").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-4) By the end of the 2018–19 season, the team reached 169 goals scored.

[![Image 93](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Chelsea_vs_Man_City_2019-02-24.svg/250px-Chelsea_vs_Man_City_2019-02-24.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chelsea_vs_Man_City_2019-02-24.svg)

Line-ups for the [2019 EFL Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_EFL_Cup_final "2019 EFL Cup final") between Chelsea and Manchester City

On 24 February, City won their sixth [League Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup") title when they defeated [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C "Chelsea F.C") 4–3 on penalties after a goalless draw over 120 minutes at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-5)

Expectations were high for City's [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League") campaign. The team again won their group without breaking a sweat, then routed [Schalke 04](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Schalke_04 "FC Schalke 04") in the round of 16, winning their home match 7–0. Similar to the previous season, City were drawn against an English club in the quarter-finals, this time [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."). _The Blues_ dropped their away match 0–1, with [Sergio Agüero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ag%C3%BCero "Sergio Agüero") missing a penalty. The home match was all-or-nothing for City and it proved to be one of the best matches of that season. [Raheem Sterling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raheem_Sterling "Raheem Sterling") scored in the beginning, but City quickly conceded two goals and now needed to score three to advance. The squad did exactly that, leading 4–2 with 20 minutes to play. However, [Fernando Llorente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Llorente "Fernando Llorente")'s contentious goal for Spurs meant City again needed a goal.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-6) In added time, Sterling converted a pass from Agüero and the entire stadium started celebrating what seemed to be a certain victory. However, the goal was disallowed after a VAR review and _the Blues_ were eliminated in a heartbreaking fashion.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-7)

The 2018–19 Premier League title race was one of the closest contests of the Premier League era. City and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") exchanged their leads 32 times over the season, in part due to fixture rearrangements for [EFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Cup "2018–19 EFL Cup") and [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_FA_Cup "2018–19 FA Cup") matches and television demands. The two title contenders jointly amassed a combined total of 195 points, which at the time was the highest combined total in English top flight history.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-8)

On 12 May, City won their final league match of the league season 4–1 away at [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.") to retain the Premier League title. In doing so, they matched their own record for 32 wins over a single season. They had to win their final 14 consecutive league matches to hold off the challenge of Liverpool, who themselves ended their season with nine-straight wins.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-9)

One week later, on 18 May, City defeated [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") 6–0 at Wembley [to win the FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_FA_Cup_Final "2019 FA Cup Final") and complete an unprecedented English men's [domestic treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Domestic_trebles "Treble (association football)") and clean sweep of the major honors in English football. It was also City's first ever league and FA Cup [double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)") and their sixth overall FA Cup title. The 6–0 scoreline was also the joint largest winning margin in the history of the FA Cup Final and the largest for any final in the competition since [1903](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1903_FA_Cup_Final "1903 FA Cup Final").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-10) This final win of the season was Manchester City's 50th in all competitions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Manchester_City_F.C._season#cite_note-11)

As of 9 April 2019, Manchester City had won the Carabao Cup, progressed to the final of the FA Cup, were in second place with one game in hand in the Premier League and scheduled to play Tottenham in the Champions League quarter-finals, thus making it possible to achieve the [quadruple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_association_football_teams_to_have_won_four_or_more_trophies_in_one_season "List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season"), a unique sweep of four major tournaments in a single season, something that had not been done by any English men's side. A win in each of City’s last twelve games of the season (potential UCL semi-finals and [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2019 UEFA Champions League Final") included) would have guaranteed the quadruple for the club. However, a dramatic loss to Tottenham on away goals on 17 April ended City's quadruple hopes. Still, the Blues managed to achieve an unprecedented domestic treble.

The 2018–19 season was Tottenham Hotspur's 27th season in the Premier League and 41st successive season in the top division of the English football league system. Along with the league, the club competed in the FA Cup, EFL Cup and UEFA Champions League.

The club finished fourth in the Premier League, qualifying for next season's Champions League, and were eliminated by Crystal Palace in the fourth round of the FA Cup. Additionally, they reached the semi-finals of the EFL Cup where they faced Chelsea. After two legs the aggregate score was 2–2 and Spurs were eliminated 4–2 on penalties. However, after overcoming Ajax on away goals after two very dramatic legs in the semi-finals, Tottenham reached the Champions League final for the first time in the club's history. In an all-English affair, Tottenham lost 0–2 to Liverpool at the Wanda Metropolitano in Madrid.

Notably, the club made no signings during both the summer and January transfer windows. This was the first time in Premier League history where this has been done.[1][2]

For the majority of the season, the club's matches were played at Wembley Stadium due to the development of the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On 3 April 2019, the new stadium opened, with the first match being a Premier League game against Crystal Palace. Tottenham won 2–0, with Son Heung-min scoring the first goal at their new ground.

The 2018–19 season was Tottenham Hotspur's 27th season in the Premier League and 41st successive season in the top division of the English football league system. Along with the league, the club competed in the FA Cup, EFL Cup and UEFA Champions League.

The club finished fourth in the Premier League, qualifying for next season's Champions League, and were eliminated by Crystal Palace in the fourth round of the FA Cup. Additionally, they reached the semi-finals of the EFL Cup where they faced Chelsea. After two legs the aggregate score was 2–2 and Spurs were eliminated 4–2 on penalties. However, after overcoming Ajax on away goals after two very dramatic legs in the semi-finals, Tottenham reached the Champions League final for the first time in the club's history. In an all-English affair, Tottenham lost 0–2 to Liverpool at the Wanda Metropolitano in Madrid.

Notably, the club made no signings during both the summer and January transfer windows. This was the first time in Premier League history where this has been done.[1][2]

For the majority of the season, the club's matches were played at Wembley Stadium due to the development of the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On 3 April 2019, the new stadium opened, with the first match being a Premier League game against Crystal Palace. Tottenham won 2–0, with Son Heung-min scoring the first goal at their new ground.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The **group stage** of the **[2013–14 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League")** was played from 17 September to 11 December 2013. A total of 32 teams competed in the group stage.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-1)

## Draw

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Draw")]

The draw was held on 29 August 2013, 17:45 [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time") ([UTC+2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC+02:00 "UTC+02:00")), at the [Grimaldi Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimaldi_Forum "Grimaldi Forum"), [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-2) The 32 teams were allocated into four pots based on their [UEFA club coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_coefficient "UEFA club coefficient") at the beginning of the season, with the title holders being placed in Pot 1 automatically. They were drawn into eight groups of four containing one team from each of the four seeding pots, with the restriction that teams from the same national association could not be drawn against each other. Moreover, the draw was controlled for teams from the same association in order to split the teams evenly into the two sets of groups (A–D, E–H) for maximum television coverage.

The fixtures were decided after the draw. On each matchday, four groups played their matches on Tuesday, while the other four groups played their matches on Wednesday, with the two sets of groups (A–D, E–H) alternating between each matchday. There were other restrictions, e.g., teams from the same city (e.g., [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C."), [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") and [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid")) in general did not play at home on the same matchday (UEFA tried to avoid teams from the same city playing at home on the same day or on consecutive days), and Russian teams did not play at home on the last matchday due to cold weather.

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Format")]

In each group, teams played against each other home-and-away in a [round-robin format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"). The group winners and runners-up advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"), while the third-placed teams entered the [Europa League round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2013–14 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-1)

### Tiebreakers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tiebreakers")]

The teams are ranked according to [points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, 0 points for a loss). If two or more teams are equal on points on completion of the group matches, the following criteria are applied to determine the rankings:[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-1)

1.   higher number of points obtained in the group matches played among the teams in question;
2.   superior [goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference") from the group matches played among the teams in question;
3.   higher number of goals scored in the group matches played among the teams in question;
4.   higher number of [goals scored away from home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") in the group matches played among the teams in question;
5.   If, after applying criteria 1 to 4 to several teams, two teams still have an equal ranking, criteria 1 to 4 are reapplied exclusively to the matches between the two teams in question to determine their final rankings. If this procedure does not lead to a decision, criteria 6 to 8 apply;
6.   superior goal difference from all group matches played;
7.   higher number of goals scored from all group matches played;
8.   higher number of [coefficient points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_coefficient "UEFA club coefficient") accumulated by the club in question, as well as its association, over the previous five seasons.
