From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The **group stage** of the **[2013–14 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League")** was played from 17 September to 11 December 2013. A total of 32 teams competed in the group stage.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-1)

## Draw

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Draw")]

The draw was held on 29 August 2013, 17:45 [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time") ([UTC+2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC+02:00 "UTC+02:00")), at the [Grimaldi Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimaldi_Forum "Grimaldi Forum"), [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-2) The 32 teams were allocated into four pots based on their [UEFA club coefficients](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_coefficient "UEFA club coefficient") at the beginning of the season, with the title holders being placed in Pot 1 automatically. They were drawn into eight groups of four containing one team from each of the four seeding pots, with the restriction that teams from the same national association could not be drawn against each other. Moreover, the draw was controlled for teams from the same association in order to split the teams evenly into the two sets of groups (A–D, E–H) for maximum television coverage.

The fixtures were decided after the draw. On each matchday, four groups played their matches on Tuesday, while the other four groups played their matches on Wednesday, with the two sets of groups (A–D, E–H) alternating between each matchday. There were other restrictions, e.g., teams from the same city (e.g., [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C."), [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") and [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C."), [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") and [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid")) in general did not play at home on the same matchday (UEFA tried to avoid teams from the same city playing at home on the same day or on consecutive days), and Russian teams did not play at home on the last matchday due to cold weather.

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Format")]

In each group, teams played against each other home-and-away in a [round-robin format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"). The group winners and runners-up advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase "2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase"), while the third-placed teams entered the [Europa League round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Europa_League_knockout_phase "2013–14 UEFA Europa League knockout phase").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-1)

### Tiebreakers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tiebreakers")]

The teams are ranked according to [points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, 0 points for a loss). If two or more teams are equal on points on completion of the group matches, the following criteria are applied to determine the rankings:[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#cite_note-regulations-1)

1.   higher number of points obtained in the group matches played among the teams in question;
2.   superior [goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference") from the group matches played among the teams in question;
3.   higher number of goals scored in the group matches played among the teams in question;
4.   higher number of [goals scored away from home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") in the group matches played among the teams in question;
5.   If, after applying criteria 1 to 4 to several teams, two teams still have an equal ranking, criteria 1 to 4 are reapplied exclusively to the matches between the two teams in question to determine their final rankings. If this procedure does not lead to a decision, criteria 6 to 8 apply;
6.   superior goal difference from all group matches played;
7.   higher number of goals scored from all group matches played;
8.   higher number of [coefficient points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_club_coefficient "UEFA club coefficient") accumulated by the club in question, as well as its association, over the previous five seasons.

The **2018–19 Ligue 1** season, also known as **Ligue 1 [Conforama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conforama "Conforama")** for sponsorship reasons, was the 81st season since its establishment. The season began on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 24 May 2019. [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.") were the defending champions.

On 21 April, Paris Saint-Germain won their second consecutive Ligue 1 title and eighth title overall following [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille_OSC "Lille OSC")'s 0–0 draw against [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse_FC "Toulouse FC").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ligue_1#cite_note-3)

Twenty teams competed in the league, with two promoted teams from [Ligue 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Ligue_2 "2017–18 Ligue 2"), [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_Reims "Stade de Reims") and [Nîmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%AEmes_Olympique "Nîmes Olympique"), replacing the two relegated teams from the [2017–18 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Ligue_1 "2017–18 Ligue 1") season, [Troyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troyes_AC "Troyes AC") and [Metz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Metz "FC Metz").

The **2018–19 Ligue 1** season, also known as **Ligue 1 [Conforama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conforama "Conforama")** for sponsorship reasons, was the 81st season since its establishment. The season began on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 24 May 2019. [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.") were the defending champions.

On 21 April, Paris Saint-Germain won their second consecutive Ligue 1 title and eighth title overall following [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille_OSC "Lille OSC")'s 0–0 draw against [Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toulouse_FC "Toulouse FC").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Ligue_1#cite_note-3)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Ligue_1&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league, with two promoted teams from [Ligue 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Ligue_2 "2017–18 Ligue 2"), [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_de_Reims "Stade de Reims") and [Nîmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%AEmes_Olympique "Nîmes Olympique"), replacing the two relegated teams from the [2017–18 Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Ligue_1 "2017–18 Ligue 1") season, [Troyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troyes_AC "Troyes AC") and [Metz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Metz "FC Metz").

The **2018–19 Premier League** was the 27th [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_(sports) "Season (sports)") of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 120th season of top-flight English football overall. The season started on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 12 May 2019.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-3) Fixtures for the 2018–19 season were announced on 14 June 2018. The league was contested by the top 17 teams from the 2017–18 season as well as [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C."), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), who joined as the promoted clubs from the [2017–18 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). They replaced [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_F.C. "Swansea City F.C.") and [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") who were relegated to the [2018–19 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship").[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-4)

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") were the defending champions, and they won their fourth Premier League title, and sixth English top-flight title overall, retaining the title on the last day of the season with 98 points after winning their last 14 league games. [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") finished second with 97 points – the highest total in English top-flight history for a second-placed team.

## Summary

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") claimed the league title on the last day of the season with a 4–1 win at [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C."), finishing on 98 points after a run of 14 straight wins.[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-5)[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") held a 7-point lead over Manchester City on 3 January,[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-6) but finished runners-up with 97 points – the fourth highest total in Premier League history and the highest in English top-flight history for a second-placed team, having lost only one league match all season – to eventual champions City.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

[Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") claimed the other two Champions League berths, finishing in third and fourth place respectively. Tottenham were in third place for much of the season and were considered potential title challengers until a 1–2 loss to [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") in February.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Chelsea would go on to win the season's [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018-19_UEFA_Europa_League "2018-19 UEFA Europa League"), defeating [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in the final 4–1. Arsenal had gone on a fourteen-game unbeaten run near the start of the season and began April in third place, but a run of four points in six matches saw them drop to fifth place, finishing outside of the Champions League spots.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

[Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.")'s worst start to the season for 28 years and 3–1 loss to Liverpool led to the sacking of manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") in December,[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-10) with former player [Ole Gunnar Solskjær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Gunnar_Solskj%C3%A6r "Ole Gunnar Solskjær") replacing him, initially as a caretaker. Solskjær was appointed permanently after an impressive run of results which culminated in United's away goals victory over [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint_Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint Germain F.C.") in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"),[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-11) but the team's poor form soon returned, and they eventually finished sixth after the team had won none of their final five league matches.[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-12) Newly promoted [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") achieved their highest finish since 1980 by finishing seventh, having taken points off every team in the league except Liverpool and [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C.").[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-13) Their seventh-place finish was the highest for a newly promoted team since [Ipswich Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich_Town_F.C. "Ipswich Town F.C.") finished 5th in the [2000–01 season.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_in_English_football "2000–01 in English football")[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-14)

Huddersfield were the first team to be relegated, following their 0–2 defeat at [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C.") on 30 March 2019, coinciding with victories for [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."). They were relegated with six games remaining. This made Huddersfield the second team in Premier League history to be relegated before March ended, following [Derby County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derby_County_F.C. "Derby County F.C.") in [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Premier_League "2007–08 Premier League").[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-15) Fulham joined them after a 1–4 defeat at [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") on 2 April, relegated with five games remaining.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-16)[Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") were the final team to be relegated following a 2–3 loss at home to Crystal Palace on 4 May with one game remaining.[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-17)

The fastest goal in Premier League history was scored this season on 23 April by [Shane Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Long "Shane Long") in a 1–1 draw between his side [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") and [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") after 7.69 seconds.[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-19) On 4 May 2019, Fulham's [Harvey Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Elliott "Harvey Elliott") became the youngest ever Premier League player at 16 years and 30 days.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-20) Tottenham Hotspur had a run of 28 games without a draw (20 wins, 8 losses), the longest ever recorded from the start of a Premier League season.[[21]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-21) Manchester City finished the season without a draw in any of their final 30 matches.

The season saw two aviation incidents involving Premier League personnel. On 27 October 2018, [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") owner [Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichai_Srivaddhanaprabha "Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha") was killed in a [helicopter crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Leicester_helicopter_crash "2018 Leicester helicopter crash") outside the [King Power Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Power_Stadium "King Power Stadium"), shortly after a 1–1 home draw against [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."). Almost three months later, on 21 January 2019, Cardiff City player [Emiliano Sala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Sala "Emiliano Sala"), en route to join the club following [his record signing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_Emiliano_Sala_from_FC_Nantes_to_Cardiff_City_F.C. "Transfer of Emiliano Sala from FC Nantes to Cardiff City F.C.") from [Nantes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Nantes "FC Nantes"), died on board a Piper PA-46 Malibu aircraft that [crashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Piper_PA-46_Malibu_crash "2019 Piper PA-46 Malibu crash") off [Alderney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderney "Alderney").[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-BBC-22)

## Teams

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). The promoted teams were [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") (returning after a six-year absence), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") (both teams returning after a four-year absence). They replaced [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C."), [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") and [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), who were relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship") after their top flight spells of seven, ten and eight years respectively.

The **2018–19 Premier League** was the 27th [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_(sports) "Season (sports)") of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League"), the top English professional league for [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") clubs, since its establishment in 1992, and the 120th season of top-flight English football overall. The season started on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 12 May 2019.[[2]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-2)[[3]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-3) Fixtures for the 2018–19 season were announced on 14 June 2018. The league was contested by the top 17 teams from the 2017–18 season as well as [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C."), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), who joined as the promoted clubs from the [2017–18 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). They replaced [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_F.C. "Swansea City F.C.") and [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") who were relegated to the [2018–19 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship").[[4]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-4)

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") were the defending champions, and they won their fourth Premier League title, and sixth English top-flight title overall, retaining the title on the last day of the season with 98 points after winning their last 14 league games. [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") finished second with 97 points – the highest total in English top-flight history for a second-placed team.

## Summary

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") claimed the league title on the last day of the season with a 4–1 win at [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C."), finishing on 98 points after a run of 14 straight wins.[[5]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-5)[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") held a 7-point lead over Manchester City on 3 January,[[6]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-6) but finished runners-up with 97 points – the fourth highest total in Premier League history and the highest in English top-flight history for a second-placed team, having lost only one league match all season – to eventual champions City.[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

[Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") claimed the other two Champions League berths, finishing in third and fourth place respectively. Tottenham were in third place for much of the season and were considered potential title challengers until a 1–2 loss to [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") in February.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-8) Chelsea would go on to win the season's [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018-19_UEFA_Europa_League "2018-19 UEFA Europa League"), defeating [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in the final 4–1. Arsenal had gone on a fourteen-game unbeaten run near the start of the season and began April in third place, but a run of four points in six matches saw them drop to fifth place, finishing outside of the Champions League spots.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-9)

[Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.")'s worst start to the season for 28 years and 3–1 loss to Liverpool led to the sacking of manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") in December,[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-10) with former player [Ole Gunnar Solskjær](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Gunnar_Solskj%C3%A6r "Ole Gunnar Solskjær") replacing him, initially as a caretaker. Solskjær was appointed permanently after an impressive run of results which culminated in United's away goals victory over [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint_Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint Germain F.C.") in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"),[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-11) but the team's poor form soon returned, and they eventually finished sixth after the team had won none of their final five league matches.[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-12) Newly promoted [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") achieved their highest finish since 1980 by finishing seventh, having taken points off every team in the league except Liverpool and [Huddersfield Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huddersfield_Town_A.F.C. "Huddersfield Town A.F.C.").[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-13) Their seventh-place finish was the highest for a newly promoted team since [Ipswich Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich_Town_F.C. "Ipswich Town F.C.") finished 5th in the [2000–01 season.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_in_English_football "2000–01 in English football")[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-14)

Huddersfield were the first team to be relegated, following their 0–2 defeat at [Crystal Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crystal_Palace_F.C. "Crystal Palace F.C.") on 30 March 2019, coinciding with victories for [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") and [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C."). They were relegated with six games remaining. This made Huddersfield the second team in Premier League history to be relegated before March ended, following [Derby County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derby_County_F.C. "Derby County F.C.") in [2007–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Premier_League "2007–08 Premier League").[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-15) Fulham joined them after a 1–4 defeat at [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") on 2 April, relegated with five games remaining.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-16)[Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") were the final team to be relegated following a 2–3 loss at home to Crystal Palace on 4 May with one game remaining.[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-17)

The fastest goal in Premier League history was scored this season on 23 April by [Shane Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Long "Shane Long") in a 1–1 draw between his side [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") and [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") after 7.69 seconds.[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-19) On 4 May 2019, Fulham's [Harvey Elliott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Elliott "Harvey Elliott") became the youngest ever Premier League player at 16 years and 30 days.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-20) Tottenham Hotspur had a run of 28 games without a draw (20 wins, 8 losses), the longest ever recorded from the start of a Premier League season.[[21]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-21) Manchester City finished the season without a draw in any of their final 30 matches.

The season saw two aviation incidents involving Premier League personnel. On 27 October 2018, [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") owner [Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichai_Srivaddhanaprabha "Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha") was killed in a [helicopter crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Leicester_helicopter_crash "2018 Leicester helicopter crash") outside the [King Power Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Power_Stadium "King Power Stadium"), shortly after a 1–1 home draw against [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."). Almost three months later, on 21 January 2019, Cardiff City player [Emiliano Sala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emiliano_Sala "Emiliano Sala"), en route to join the club following [his record signing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transfer_of_Emiliano_Sala_from_FC_Nantes_to_Cardiff_City_F.C. "Transfer of Emiliano Sala from FC Nantes to Cardiff City F.C.") from [Nantes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Nantes "FC Nantes"), died on board a Piper PA-46 Malibu aircraft that [crashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Piper_PA-46_Malibu_crash "2019 Piper PA-46 Malibu crash") off [Alderney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alderney "Alderney").[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League#cite_note-BBC-22)

## Teams

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2018%E2%80%9319_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_EFL_Championship "2017–18 EFL Championship"). The promoted teams were [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.") (returning after a six-year absence), [Cardiff City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiff_City_F.C. "Cardiff City F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") (both teams returning after a four-year absence). They replaced [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C."), [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C.") and [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C."), who were relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_EFL_Championship "2018–19 EFL Championship") after their top flight spells of seven, ten and eight years respectively.
